# Doncic, Mamukelashvili and Reaves lead Lakers past Bucks 123-112 for 7th straight win

 November 11, 2026 / 7:54 PM PST / AP 

Luka Doncic scored 32 points, Sandro Mamukelashvili added 23 and Austin Reaves 18 as the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to seven games with a 123-112 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night.

Mamukelashvili, a second-round draft pick of the Bucks in 2021, matched a season-high for points set on Monday at Atlanta, and Reaves returned to action after missing Monday's game due to illness. 

Walker Kessler had 10 points and 11 rebounds, and Collin Sexton chipped in with 10 points for Los Angeles, which improved to a league-best 11-2.

title: No Austin Reaves, no problem. Luka Doncic and Lakers beat Hawks - Los Angeles Times
text:
Lakers guard Collin Sexton celebrates during the first half of a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night.

(Mike Stewart / Associated Press)

 By Thuc Nhi Nguyen Staff Writer Follow 

Nov. 9, 2026 Updated 9:11 PM PT

- Luka Doncic finished with 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds and five steals as the Lakers defeated the Atlanta Hawks 124-114.
- Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 23 points off the bench and Walker Kessler finished with 21 points for the Lakers.

ATLANTA — Austin Reaves took the baton from Luka Doncic when Doncic sat out Sunday, and when the roles were reversed Monday, Doncic passed it to his teammates.

Doncic had 32 points and 10 assists in a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks as the Lakers relied on their depth to secure their sixth consecutive win and stay atop the Western Conference despite a short, tired bench.

## Seven in a row, and first place

The Lakers beat the Bucks 123-112 in Milwaukee on Wednesday night. It was their seventh straight win, it finished a 3-0 road trip, and it moved them to 11-2.

That is the best record in the NBA. San Antonio, at 10-2 with 10 straight wins, is half a game behind them in the West, and Boston leads the East at 10-2.

...

The start was uneven. The Lakers won three of their first four, then lost at home to Portland 136-129 on Oct. 27 and lost 112-95 at Golden State three nights later, when they made 11 of 39 threes.

They have not lost since.
